description.p: Nuvasha Launcher keeps Minecraft installations separate, so each instance can have its own version, loader, Java runtime, settings, mods, and worlds.

Browse Modrinth to install modpacks, mods, resource packs, shaders, and per-world datapacks, or download verified Eclipse Temurin Java runtimes directly in the app. Local .mrpack files can be imported and exported, with downloads checked before they are installed.

The launcher supports vanilla Minecraft and the Fabric, Quilt, Forge, and NeoForge loaders. It supports Microsoft accounts (as well as offline accounts once a Microsoft account is added), and includes account-specific skins and capes.
Instances can be duplicated, moved, renamed, exported, and removed independently. Nuvasha Launcher is built with GTK 4 and libadwaita for Linux and is also available as a Flatpak.
NOT AN OFFICIAL MINECRAFT PRODUCT. NOT APPROVED BY OR ASSOCIATED WITH MOJANG OR MICROSOFT.

description.p: Release 2.0 adds a built-in Eclipse Temurin Java runtime downloader with automatic recommended-version detection, a per-world Modrinth datapacks browser and manager, global launch defaults with per-instance dedicated GPU, GameMode, and MangoHud toggles, live Minecraft server status and latency pings, drag-and-drop reordering for servers and worlds, direct version-picker downloads with inline spinners, transitive mod dependency tracking with an optional disable-dependents setting, instant cached icons with pack.png fallbacks, and cache/locale fixes.

Release 1.9 tightens Flatpak permissions by switching account storage to the XDG Secret Portal, runs local .mrpack imports in the background without opening the modpack browser, updates browser version-picker icons, streamlines empty states and translations, refreshes documentation, and enables headless display tests in CI.

Release 1.8 enables X11/XWayland socket access in the Flatpak sandbox so Minecraft launches on Wayland sessions, automatically fetches Modrinth titles and icons for modpack-installed content, shows Default instead of 0 for unset instance RAM, and replaces text buttons in the skin dialog with right-aligned import and export icon buttons.

Release 1.7 adds multi-selection checkboxes and batch installation with dependency resolution for mods, resource packs, shaders, and modpacks, fixes modpack instance icon downloads, simplifies browser row interactions, and adds automatic Java runtime discovery in the launcher data directory.

Release 1.6 modernizes dialogs and the main window according to GNOME Human Interface Guidelines (HIG), introduces in-app toast feedback, strengthens secret store persistence for accounts, and synchronizes translation catalogs.

Release 1.5 streamlines UI interactions by removing multi-selection overhead, offloads JSON parsing and asset pre-verification to background threads, adds FICLONE copy-on-write acceleration, normalizes codebase patterns, and hardens tests.

Release 1.4 adds instance sidebar groups and an instance Stats tab, fixes a task completion race and download cache fallback, isolates test secret storage, and speeds up builds, tests, and CI packaging.

Release 1.3 replaces the main window edit mode with direct row multi-selection and a per-row Settings button, adds a Java Memory (MiB) setting with custom -Xmx precedence, adds multi-selection to Worlds and Servers tabs, improves search bars and empty-state centering, adds --list-worlds and --list-servers CLI flags, and renames the binary to nuvashalauncher.

Release 1.2 adds Worlds and Servers tabs with NBT support and QuickPlay direct launch, lazy-loaded version lists, unified top header bar controls and search across instance tabs, CLI QuickPlay options (--server and --world), and packaging/CI fixes.

Release 1.1 focuses on performance, caching, and reduced disk and network overhead across the launcher. Highlights include API cache support for the Mojang version manifest, Modrinth request deduplication and batched update checks, parallel Java runtime probing off the main thread, single-pass archive metadata and cached local icon extraction, coalesced content index writes, GFileMonitor-based instance directory tracking, and debounced search and category filtering.

Release 1.0 brings Linux distribution packaging (RPM, Debian/Ubuntu, Arch Linux, and NixOS flake) with NixOS store Java discovery. This release also introduces modern 64px loading spinners, external link and export symbolic action icons, streamlined distribution dependencies, comprehensive unit test coverage reaching over 70% of the backend codebase, and an exhaustive audit fixing async task lifetimes, memory management, 3D skin rendering, archive and filesystem security, OAuth, and launcher stability.

Improved error handling throughout the launcher. User-facing errors are now localized across account management, instances, Java and loaders, Minecraft launching, content browsing, modpacks, skins, and settings. Technical failures are presented with clear translated summaries, hidden errors are revealed, and temporary authentication or invalid-download failures are handled more safely.

Account records now use the desktop Secret Service, preserving offline and Microsoft identities, tokens, cosmetics, and active-account state. This release also improves account persistence tests, headless test handling, and sanitizer cleanup.
Improved sign-in, content navigation, instance version handling, and skin previews. This release also strengthens archive safety, download cleanup, Java discovery, and test coverage.

Unified technical branding under the nuvashalauncher application ID, added CLI flags and Bash completion for managing instances and accounts, cached skin and cape previews per session, hardened archive and filesystem path validation, and split large modules and test suites.
Added Flatpak packaging for the GNOME 51 runtime, shared custom Java runtime directories across instances, reported Java vendor names, and removed the legacy nested Bubblewrap sandbox.

Added instance and content edit modes with multi-selection, bulk duplicate/delete/export actions, persistent drag-and-drop instance reordering, circular icons, and a cancellable Update All progress popover.

Renamed the project to Nuvasha Launcher, migrated UI templates to GResource and preferences to GSettings, added Minecraft skin and cape synchronization, CLI instance launching, live log auto-scrolling, and architecture documentation.
Added an OpenGL 3D skin preview renderer, redesigned the account skin manager with legacy skin support, added X11 display backend support alongside Wayland, and expanded multi-distribution CI.

Initial release featuring isolated Minecraft instances, Mojang version resolution, Fabric/Quilt/Forge/NeoForge loader installation, Modrinth browsing and .mrpack import/export, Microsoft and offline accounts, automatic Java discovery, and translations across 22 languages.
